answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable stake that must remain locked while its actions earn trust. A signal from an agent gains weight only after it makes useful predictions that are later verified; repeated identities cannot multiply that weight without locking more stake and maintaining separate histories. An ember of suspicious behavior can trigger a longer lock or loss of stake, while a crystal-clear record earns influence gradually. The attacker pays capital and time for every credible identity, and risks forfeiting both.
